acceptance.output_evidence: (1) WHICH CAPTURED RESPONSES HAD TO BE EXTENDED, AND HOW THE FIRST LIVE RUN COULD DIFFER. FIVE, not the two the criterion names, and all five are separated from the measured ones in fixtures/har/FIXTURE_MANIFEST.json under the key what_is_EXTENDED_rather_than_measured, so a reader does not have to trust this paragraph to tell them apart. (i) THE UPLOAD RESPONSE BODY. The live cloud run recorded the response KEY SET and the TYPES (status, errors, rows, weight, upload_record_id, isExtractedHoldings); the encrypted upload.json is not in this repo. The row VALUES here (SPY 60000, AGG 40000, the ids) are reconstructed to that shape. HOW THE FIRST LIVE RUN COULD DIFFER: step_upload() RECONCILES rather than parses -- it requires the echoed row count to equal what was sent, weight == 'Dollars', and an INT upload_record_id. If the vendor echoes rows in a different order, coerces the unit label, returns upload_record_id as a string, or silently drops an unmatched row, the live run REFUSES where the replay proceeds. That is the designed behaviour and it is also the untested path. The shape this cell would NOT survive silently is the dangerous one -- a partial upload reported as a success -- and it is precisely what the reconciliation exists to catch. (ii) THE TWO-COMPARISON-ONLY MULTI EXAMPLE. Template 14141847 is declared to take 2..5 comparison securities, and every capture available anywhere carries exactly TWO. So the 3, 4 and 5-comparison cases are enforced BY RULE (VARIANT_BY_COUNT, and the battery shows a 6-comparison request selecting no recipe) and EXERCISED BY NOTHING. HOW THE FIRST LIVE RUN COULD DIFFER: the comparisonSecurities array is the only carrier that grows, but the vendor may also key layout, page count or the duplicate cover fields off the comparison count -- the CRO's live 14141847 run measured 35 pages landscape AT TWO COMPARISONS, and nothing in this estate knows what five produces. A 3..5 request is the first live test of its own body shape. (iii) THE PORTFOLIO COLLECTION LISTING. NO listing was captured anywhere. The GET /model_portfolios/fixed/ body is CONSTRUCTED so the reconciliation arm has a population with a newer foreign row in it. Its SHAPE is a guess about the listing endpoint -- which matters more than the other four, because reconciliation-after-an-uncertain-create reads this endpoint and nothing else. If the live listing paginates, or filters to the caller's own rows, or names the portfolio field differently, reconcile_owned() finds no candidate and the job goes to ATTENTION rather than adopting wrongly -- the safe direction, and still a failure the replay cannot show. (iv) THE STATUS READ-BACK. No /model_portfolios/{id}/status body was captured; the live run recorded only that a later GET returned status 'available'. The effective-settings field names here are the CREATE body's names echoed back. If the vendor renames them on read, the read-back reports drift on all seven and the job goes to ATTENTION -- a false ATTENTION, which is the one failure mode in this cell that is noisy rather than silent, and is therefore the acceptable one. (v) THE PDF. A 193-byte synthetic PDF, not the live 23-page 573,643-byte artifact. It is valid by header, EOF and size, which is what the download path checks; page-level certification against a paired PDF is cell IB-s-10's, which is why extraction_validation.status is recorded UNCERTIFIED here rather than CERTIFIED. ONE CROSS-CUTTING DIFFERENCE THE CRITERION DOES NOT ASK ABOUT BUT THE CVO SHOULD WEIGH: the replay's session is STUBBED. B8 owns acquisition, the fence and publication; this cell reads a fenced session BY NAME and never mints one. Every 401/eviction/WAF branch in the decision table is therefore exercised against an INJECTED signal, not a real one -- and the WAF branch is the one where that matters most, because row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S8 shows the carried classifier could not see the case the live run actually produced. (2) WHAT 'UNCERTAIN CREATE' CASES THE REPLAY CANNOT PRODUCE. The replay can inject a kill (arm (b)) and can return a null status (the RECONCILE branch). Both are DETERMINISTIC and both are raised on the CLIENT side. It cannot produce: (i) THE GENUINE AMBIGUITY -- the vendor's write landed and the response was lost on a network this test does not own. Arm (b)'s kill is injected at a point the test CHOOSES, so the test always knows the mutation executed; the live case is exactly the one where nobody knows. The job is built for it (HTTP class alone never proves a mutation did not execute; it reconciles before any replay) and that belief is unexercised against a real loss. (ii) THE PARTIAL WRITE -- a portfolio row created with some items and not others, or created and then rolled back vendor-side. Reconciliation asks 'does a row with my deterministic name exist', which is a BOOLEAN; it does not ask 'is that row COMPLETE'. A half-written portfolio adopted by name would then be generated from. This is the sharpest gap in this cell and I am naming it rather than leaving it to be found. (iii) THE CONCURRENT CREATE -- two Opal workers claiming the same request. The conditional claim_intent is exercised single-process; DynamoDB's conditional-write semantics are asserted, not observed, because the replay's JobStore is in memory. (iv) A NAME COLLISION WITH A HUMAN. The opaque deterministic name is this cell's whole identity mechanism. The replay guarantees it is unique because the replay populates the collection. Live, an advisor working in the YCharts UI can create a portfolio with any name at all, and nothing reserves this cell's namespace vendor-side. (v) A VENDOR-SIDE TIMEOUT INSIDE THE 26.76 s WINDOW. The measured Overview invocation is 26.76 s against a 900 s Lambda budget -- 33.6x headroom, so the durable-worker branch is NOT selected and NOT exercised. If Comparison or Multi (31 and 35 pages against Overview's 23) scale super-linearly, that selection is the first thing that changes, and the branch it would select has never run. (3) WHAT AN OPERATOR SEES WHEN A STEP FAILS MID-CHAIN. The job carries eight states (CLAIMED, SUBMITTING, SUBMITTED, UNCERTAIN, DOWNLOADING, READY, FAILED, ATTENTION) and a failure lands in one of the last three, never in an ambiguous silence. FAILED is a terminal refusal with a code and no vendor cost -- the four pre-access controls (CLIENT_ACCOUNT_SCOPE_MISMATCH, CHANGED_INPUTS_SAME_REQUEST_ID, COMPARISON_OUTSIDE_AUTHORIZED_CATALOG, SERVER_CONTROLLED_FIELD) and the 17 envelope refusals all resolve here, each measured at 0 vendor requests. The operator sees WHICH input was refused by NAME and never the refused VALUE (arm (amend): 0 occurrences over the whole envelope). ATTENTION is the state that needs a person and cannot be retried into correctness: SETTINGS_DRIFTED (the vendor's effective settings disagree with what the request asked for -- the job does NOT proceed to READY and does NOT 'fix' the drift, because the number's meaning changed), repeat eviction after the one allowed refresh, and a reconciliation that finds no owned row. UNCERTAIN is the state after a timeout, disconnect or ambiguous 5xx during a mutation. The operator sees UNCERTAIN with the stage named, and the job's own next act is to RECONCILE the owned vendor object before any replay -- a timeout NEVER licenses regeneration. WHAT THE OPERATOR DOES NOT SEE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST ANSWER TO THIS QUESTION: there is NO operator-facing surface in this cell. No route, no status envelope, no notification -- IB-s-16 owns the operations status envelope and per-tenant recovery, and the standing moratorium forbids this cell building any monitor, alarm, SNS or SES send. So the states above are what an operator WOULD see through IB-s-16's surface once it exists; today they are durable rows and log lines and nothing polls them. A partial chain therefore leaves a correct, durable, and UNATTENDED record. The CVO should weigh whether FWD-4 is served by that. Two further things an operator does not get: the artifact of a FAILED attempt is not retained (only READY attempts write under firms/<id>/generations/<id>/attempts/<a>/vendor/report.pdf), so a mid-chain failure leaves no partial PDF to inspect; and because signed URL parameters are never logged, a download failure cannot be reproduced from the logs by re-fetching the URL -- deliberate, and it does cost an operator the obvious diagnostic. (4) THE INSTRUMENT THIS RECORD WAS WRITTEN WITH, since a judgment is only as good as what it read. Every claim above is from the fixture manifest, the battery's 162-line output, the job's own state machine, or the reuse packets at their cited commits -- not from memory of the build. The manifest specifically was RE-DERIVED rather than read, which is the only reason the two stale rows recorded in row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S9 did not end up cited in this very paragraph as measured evidence.
